headline_marked: [[Deschamps dismisses referee controversy]] ahead of France-Morocco World Cup quarterfinal
headline: Deschamps dismisses referee controversy ahead of France-Morocco World Cup quarterfinal
summary: France coach Didier Deschamps has downplayed ongoing refereeing debates, including a contentious Argentina-Egypt match, stating his team's sole focus is their World Cup quarterfinal against Morocco. He expressed trust in the officials for the upcoming clash.
details: France coach Didier Deschamps has brushed aside fresh refereeing controversy, insisting his side's only focus is their World Cup quarterfinal against Morocco. The debate intensified after Argentina's contentious win over Egypt and FIFA's appointment of an all-Argentine officiating team for France's last-eight tie.

Deschamps refused to be drawn into speculation during Wednesday's pre-match press conference. He stated, "Our opponent is Morocco, not the referees. I trust the referees," emphasizing his team's commitment to the game.

The 57-year-old, who led France to World Cup glory in 2018, even defended French referee François Letexier. He quipped that he hoped the officials for Thursday's clash would be "as good as Monsieur Letexier was."

Deschamps reiterated that France's attention remains firmly on the pitch rather than the surrounding controversy. He urged his players to be more clinical in front of goal after their narrow last-16 victory over Paraguay.

The former France midfielder described the Moroccan side as "here to win," highlighting their strength. He also confirmed that FIFA had informed them that Michael Olise's yellow card against Paraguay would stand, despite France's appeal.

headline_marked: [[Ayatollah Ali Khamenei buried]] in Mashhad today after week-long mourning across Iran and Iraq
headline: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei buried in Mashhad today after week-long mourning across Iran and Iraq
summary: Millions gathered in Iran and Iraq to pay last respects to the former Supreme Leader, who was reportedly killed in a US-Israel attack on February 28, along with four family members.
details: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran's former Supreme Leader, was buried today in his birthplace, Mashhad, following a week-long mourning period across five cities in Iran and Iraq.
Khamenei was reportedly killed on February 28 in a US and Israeli attack, along with four members of his family. His burial was initially postponed due to the intensity of the ongoing conflict.
The decision to proceed with his burial was made after a memorandum of understanding for a permanent ceasefire was signed between Tehran and Washington.
The week-long mourning ceremonies began last Friday. Khamenei's coffin was displayed at Tehran's Grand Mosalla, then moved to Qom, and subsequently flown to neighboring Iraq.
He will be laid to rest beside the tomb of Shia Imam Reza. Mourners in Iraq paid their respects amidst renewed tensions between the US and Iran regarding the peace process.
US President Donald Trump recently declared the ceasefire over, stating that negotiations with Iran were a waste of time. This announcement followed new instability in the Strait of Hormuz.

Three ships were attacked in the waterway, with Iran denying responsibility despite accusations. US forces responded by attacking dozens of Iranian targets, leading Iran to strike US military installations in Bahrain and Kuwait.

Born in Mashhad in 1939, Khamenei spent much of his childhood and youth there, pursuing religious education before moving to Qom for higher studies. He was elected Supreme Leader in 1989, succeeding Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

Millions attended the mourning ceremonies in both Iran and Iraq. Mourners expressed profound respect for his perceived stance against the power of the United States and Israel, and his role in managing Israel.

Iraq declared a public holiday yesterday for the funeral procession, where thousands gathered in Najaf despite intense heat, attempting to touch the coffin. The procession's destination was the tomb of Hazrat Ali (RA).

Hundreds of religious leaders, adorned in white and black turbans, waited for hours to participate in Khamenei's funeral prayer inside the tomb. The coffin was then taken to Karbala, another holy city for Shia communities in Iraq.

Some participants in the procession, like Haydar Jaafar, stated they did not support Iran's policies in Iraq but attended because they believed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed by Israel and the United States.
